attackPath.dataFlow: query token -> webhook authentication; Nginx $request -> access.log -> log reader
attackPath.impact: Conditional disclosure to distinct log-reader audience; actual query usage and log access unverified.
limitations: Runtime deployment/access unverified; no registration compromise claimed.
preconditions: Operator sends secret in supported query parameter
Attacker reads edge logs without environment-secret access

confidence.rationale: Baseline source traced and validated in isolated ASGI/SQLite/private Redis reproduction.

preventiveControls: Bind credentials and resource authorization at ingress
findings.remediation: Remove query authentication; use headers/Bearer. Update configuration guidance and rotate if historical query usage is confirmed.
remediationTests: Assert malicious input rejected before dispatch or cleanup

severity.rationale: Conditional disclosure to distinct log-reader audience; actual query usage and log access unverified.

findings.summary: At baseline6c5564e valid query token authenticates HEALTH_CHECK withHTTP200; Nginx logs the entire $request including query. Log readers can obtain the shared ingress credential when an operator uses this supported transport.
findings.title: Forwarder query authentication exposes shared secret to access logs

limitations: No production access; SQLite substitutes PostgreSQL.
validation.method: Local ASGI with real SQLite/Redis and mocked external issuer

attackPath.dataFlow: manual JSON.phone + owned job -> privileged wake-up -> consume_scoped_otp -> victim keys deleted
attackPath.impact: Authenticated cross-tenant OTP availability/integrity disruption; no OTP disclosure or unauthorized issuance proven.
limitations: Runtime deployment/access unverified; no registration compromise claimed.
preconditions: Known victim phone has pending OTP keys

confidence.rationale: Baseline source traced and validated in isolated ASGI/SQLite/private Redis reproduction.

preventiveControls: Bind credentials and resource authorization at ingress
findings.remediation: Derive phone from authorized durable job/driver; validate state/challenge before dispatch and bind cleanup to that association.
remediationTests: Assert malicious input rejected before dispatch or cleanup

severity.rationale: Authenticated cross-tenant OTP availability/integrity disruption; no OTP disclosure or unauthorized issuance proven.

findings.summary: At baseline6c5564e caller phone bypasses job ownership boundary into privileged cleanup. Tenant1's owned successful job and tenant2's phone returnedHTTP200 and deleted victim Redis keys2->0. External issuer was not called.
findings.title: An owned job allows deletion of another tenant's pending OTP state

limitations: No production access; SQLite substitutes PostgreSQL.
validation.method: Local ASGI with real SQLite/Redis and mocked external issuer
